title: Enquiry to confirmed chef: how myCHEF booking works
body_markdown:
Instead of chasing menus, timings and guest details across separate messages, put your enquiry into one written brief, review the proposed service and request clear booking confirmation. For the private chef booking process in Dubai, the key distinction is between discussing a date and confirming an agreed arrangement. This guide focuses on the checks you control before a chef arrives.


**TL;DR**

- The private chef booking process Dubai clients need starts with a clear brief, not a menu alone.
- myCHEF provides vetted chefs; confirm the proposed menu, service scope and booking terms before proceeding.
- Separate recurring household cooking from one-off private dining when describing your requirements.
- Request written confirmation covering the date, location, timings, responsibilities and agreed service.


Start with the [myCHEF enquiry page](https://www.mychef.ae/contact) to describe the service you need and request a tailored proposal. Include your date, location, number of diners and whether you want recurring cooking or a single occasion.

## Why a clear booking brief matters

A menu describes the food. A booking brief also describes the work: shopping responsibilities, kitchen access, preparation, serving and the agreed finish.

If those details remain scattered across messages, you cannot easily check whether the proposed arrangement matches your expectations. Keep one current summary and ask for unresolved points to be answered before you accept.

**myCHEF private chef services suit Dubai households seeking vetted chefs for home cooking or private dining.** The useful next step is to define which service you need, rather than treating every request as the same booking.

The checklist below is a customer-side planning workflow. Your proposal and booking terms should establish the actual arrangements for your enquiry, including any payment requirements and the point at which the booking becomes confirmed.

## Before you start

You do not need an integration or a separate planning account. You need enough information for the enquiry to describe the job accurately.

- **Prepare the essentials:** your preferred date, Dubai location, number of adults and children, service required and a contact person who can approve decisions.
- **Gather the practical details:** dietary requirements, kitchen facilities, building access arrangements and any fixed serving time. Photographs of the cooking area can help explain the space if requested.
- **Resolve the easily missed distinction:** the time you want to eat is not the chef’s arrival time. Ask for arrival, preparation and service timings separately before arranging access.

For a household enquiry, describe the cooking pattern you want. For a dinner party, describe the occasion and how you want guests to be served. Guest count alone does not decide the service category.

## Your enquiry brief

### 1. Define the service and occasion

Begin with the purpose of the booking. Say whether you need regular household meals, weekly meal preparation, a private dinner or catering for a celebration.

A one-off dinner remains a private dining or catering enquiry even when it takes place in your own kitchen. Recurring cooking needs a different brief because the discussion includes schedules, preferences and how meals fit into household routines.

Use the comparison below to choose the clearest starting point. These are planning distinctions, not advertised package inclusions.

| Service format | Best for | What your brief should explain | Main limitation to resolve |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recurring household cooking | Households wanting an ongoing cooking arrangement | Preferred visit pattern, diners, meal preferences and kitchen arrangements | Visits and responsibilities need agreement rather than being assumed |
| Weekly meal preparation | Households wanting meals prepared for later use | Meals required, portion needs, containers and storage space | Preparing meals is different from serving a hosted dinner |
| Private dining | Hosts planning a single seated meal | Occasion, guest count, menu direction and serving time | Chef attendance does not by itself define table service |
| Event catering | Hosts coordinating food for a celebration or business event | Venue, service format, guest flow and staffing needs | Food, equipment and event staffing need separate scope checks |

**Choose the service by the work required, not by the label that sounds closest.** This keeps your enquiry focused and gives you a clearer basis for reviewing the response.

### 2. Record the people, place and timing

Give the date and location together. Include the building or community, the type of property and who will provide access, without publishing private access codes in a general planning document.

State the number of people eating, separating adults and children where their meals differ. Identify dietary requirements by the affected diner or group, rather than writing a broad instruction such as healthy food.

For example, an illustrative dinner brief might specify **8 diners**, including **2 children**, with a separate dietary requirement for **1 guest**. Those details describe different planning needs; they should not disappear inside a total headcount.

Include the intended meal time and any fixed point in the evening, such as a speech or cake presentation. Ask what preparation access is required rather than deciding an arrival time yourself.

### 3. Set a useful menu direction

Describe the style of meal, preferred cuisines and ingredients you do not want. Add whether you prefer shared dishes, individually plated courses or another service format.

Separate preferences from allergies and other dietary requirements. A preference can guide menu design; an allergy needs an explicit discussion about ingredients and preparation arrangements.

**Expected result:** one brief that explains what is being cooked, who will eat it, where the work happens and when the meal should be served. Keep this version available while you review the proposal.

## Your proposal review

### 4. Check the menu against the brief

Read the proposed menu alongside the latest guest details. Check that dietary alternatives are identified and that children’s meals, if requested, have not been left implicit.

Ask how the menu will be served. A list of dishes does not tell you whether food arrives at the table together, in courses or as a self-service spread.

If you request a change, ask whether it affects preparation, equipment or the agreed scope. Keep the revised menu with the booking summary so an earlier version cannot be mistaken for the final choice.

### 5. Confirm what the service includes

Ask for the proposed responsibilities in writing. Do not assume that a chef booking automatically includes groceries, waiting staff, crockery, glassware, table styling or every part of the kitchen clean-down.

Use this scope checklist:

- Who sources the ingredients, and how are substitutions agreed?
- Which equipment is supplied, and which kitchen facilities must you provide?
- Who serves dishes and clears the dining area?
- Are any additional staff included in the proposal?
- What cleaning tasks are included, and what remains your responsibility?
- How are leftovers, containers and waste handled?

These questions are not objections to the proposal. They establish the boundaries of the service before you organise the rest of the occasion around it.

### 6. Review the quote and terms together

Compare the quoted scope with your latest brief, not just the menu heading. Guest numbers, staffing, ingredients, equipment, service format and access requirements are all points to clarify when reviewing a tailored proposal.

Request the applicable payment, cancellation and amendment terms before proceeding. Ask what action confirms the booking and whether any requested date is being held during the discussion.

**Expected result:** an agreed description of the food, work and responsibilities, with the applicable terms understood. A proposal that still contains unresolved assumptions is not ready for final acceptance.

*Agree the scope before moving to confirmation and practical handover.*


## Your written confirmation and final handover

### 7. Request an explicit confirmation record

Ask for written confirmation that identifies the agreed booking. Do not treat a menu discussion, an unanswered acceptance message or a quotation alone as evidence that every detail is settled.

Your confirmation record should let you check:

- The booking date and complete service address.
- The agreed diner count and dietary requirements.
- The final menu or its clearly identified version.
- Arrival arrangements and the intended serving time.
- The agreed service scope and any additional staffing.
- The applicable terms and any outstanding actions.

Ask how chef assignment and any subsequent changes will be communicated. myCHEF provides vetted chefs, but the person attending, the agreed responsibilities and the practical arrangements still need to be clear for your particular booking.

### 8. Complete the practical handover

Give the designated contact any relevant parking, reception, lift or security instructions. Check venue procedures directly rather than assuming a chef can enter through the same route as your guests.

Describe the available hob, oven, refrigeration and preparation space accurately. Flag equipment that is not working and identify any restrictions on kitchen use before the day.

Nominate someone who can answer access questions and approve practical decisions. If that person is not the original enquirer, share the current booking summary with them.

**Expected result:** the host and service team are working from the same written arrangement. Any remaining actions have a named owner rather than being left for arrival day.

## When you need recurring household cooking

Recurring cooking uses the same brief-and-confirmation discipline, but the handover becomes a repeatable household plan. Do not simply copy a dinner-party brief and change the date.

1. **Describe the visit pattern.** Explain which days or periods suit the household and ask what arrangement can be agreed.
2. **Define the meal requirements.** State who eats at home, which meals need preparation and which preferences should remain consistent.
3. **Agree household responsibilities.** Clarify ingredient sourcing, containers, storage space and access for each visit.
4. **Set a change process.** Ask how to communicate travel, guest visits, revised portions or a change in dietary requirements.

The benefit is continuity: the household has a stable reference for what it wants prepared. The trade-off is that recurring arrangements need an agreed method for updates; an old meal plan should not silently become the instruction for a changed week.

**Expected result:** a repeatable brief with a clear route for amendments, rather than a fresh set of disconnected instructions before every visit.

## Booking problems to resolve before the day

### The serving time has been mistaken for arrival time

Ask for both times to be written separately. Then confirm when the kitchen and building access must be available; the dinner start alone does not answer either question.

### The guest count changes after menu approval

Send the revised count and identify any change in dietary requirements. Request an updated written response covering the menu, service scope and any effect on the quotation before treating the amendment as accepted.

### An allergy appears only in a passing message

Move the requirement into the main brief and request explicit acknowledgement. Discuss the relevant ingredients and preparation arrangements; do not substitute a preference label for an allergy discussion.

### You expected table service, but the proposal is unclear

Ask who plates, carries, serves and clears each part of the meal. If you want dedicated waiting staff, state that requirement directly and request a revised scope where needed.

### Several people are giving different instructions

Choose one decision-maker and circulate one current summary. Ask everyone else to send proposed changes through that person so the menu, guest count and timings do not diverge.

## FAQ


**How do I start the private chef booking process in Dubai?**

Start with a written enquiry stating your date, location, diner count and service required. Add dietary requirements, menu preferences and the intended serving time so the proposal addresses the actual work.

**When is my private chef booking confirmed?**

Treat the booking as confirmed only when the provider explicitly confirms it under the applicable booking terms. Ask what action is required and keep the written confirmation with your final menu and service details.

**Does a private chef booking include groceries and equipment?**

Do not assume groceries and equipment are included. Ask the proposal to identify ingredient sourcing, supplied equipment and the kitchen facilities you must provide.

**Can I book a chef for one dinner rather than regular visits?**

myCHEF provides dinner-party services as well as recurring household cooking and weekly meal preparation. Describe a single dinner as a private dining enquiry so the discussion covers the occasion, menu and service format.

**Should I share allergies before choosing the menu?**

Yes, include allergies in the initial brief and discuss the preparation requirements before approving the menu. Request explicit acknowledgement and keep the requirement in the final booking summary.

**What happens if my guest count changes?**

Send the revised count and ask for written acceptance of the amendment. Check whether the change affects the menu, staffing, equipment or quotation rather than assuming the original arrangement still applies.

**Do I need to be home when the chef arrives?**

Agree access arrangements before the booking day. If another person will admit the chef, give that person the current instructions and ensure a decision-maker can be contacted.

## Your next step

Before accepting a proposal, read the booking summary as if you were the person opening the door. If you cannot tell when the chef arrives, what is being prepared and who handles service, request those details first.

For a tailored myCHEF enquiry, send your **date, Dubai location, guest count and service required**. Add your menu direction, dietary requirements and intended serving time, and ask for the scope and confirmation requirements in writing.
